name: Total value of a fills file
brief:
A venue sends its fills as text, one fill per line in the form `qty,price`. `qty` is a whole number of shares, with a leading `-` for a sale. `price` is whole pence, digits only. A fill is worth `qty * price`.

Write `fills_value(text)`, which returns the total value of the good rows. Skip every bad row: an empty line, a row without exactly one comma, an empty field, or any other character (a space or a `+` makes the row bad). Lines end with `
`, some files use `
` (drop a `` at the end of a line), and the last line may have no ending.

For `"100,2510
-40,2490
qty,price
"` the first row is worth 251,000, the second -99,600, and the header is a bad row. The answer is 151,400.
constraints: The text has at most 10,000 lines. A good row has $|$`qty`$| \le 10^6$ and `price` $\le 10^7$.
The total can pass 2,147,483,647, so it needs a `long long`.
There is no `try` in the runner: check each character yourself instead of calling `std::stoi`.
hint: Split the text into lines yourself, then each line at its commas. `c - '0'` turns a digit character `c` into its value.

examples.note: 251,000 less 99,600; the header row is skipped.

how: Submit runs 13 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: Each line is checked on its own, so one bad row costs only that row.
A last line with no `\n` is still a row: the loop treats the end of the text as one more line end.
The value of one row reaches $10^{13}$, so both the product and the total are `long long`.

planted.slip: Only a line ended by a newline is read, so a last line with no ending is lost.
Reads digits up to the first bad character, as atoi does, so 12x counts as 12.
The running total is an int and overflows on a large file.
